Author: Saurabh Shyam Shamshery

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 1951 of 2023
Applicant :- Rajkumar

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Kunjesh Kumar Dubey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ajay Kumar Srivastava Hon'ble Saurabh Shyam Shamshery,J.

1. Heard Sri K.K. Dubey, learned counsel for applicant, Sri Rishi Chaddha, learned AGA for State and Sri Atul Kumar Srivastava, Advocate holding brief of Sri Ajay Kumar Srivastava, Advocate for Informant.
2.

Applicant-Rajkumar has approached this Court by way of filing present bail application seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 210 of 2022, under Sections 452, 323, 354, 504, 376, 511 IPC,
Police Station Mundha Pandey, District Moradabad, after rejection of his bail application vide order dated 02.01.2023 passed by Sessions Judge, Moradabad.
3.
Victim, a widow, initially lodged FIR against applicant and co-accused that applicant (husband of a Gram Pradhan) has enmity with her.

He alongwith co-accused came to her house, assaulted her son and also outraged her modesty.
Rajkumar vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124661895/
1 4.
Learned counsel for applicant submits that during investigation victim has improved her case and added that applicant and co-accused also attempted offence of rape.
Same version was repeated by victim in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. with further addition that it was third time, as such, it is a case of false implication.
FIR was lodged with a delay of three days which remained unexplained.
Medico legal examination of victim shows that she suffered a simple injury.
Learned counsel further submits that applicant?s wife has lodged FIR against informant and others that they have assaulted her and her husband and both received incised wounds.
There are major contradictions in statement of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.

Learned counsel also submits that applicant has no criminal history and he is languishing in jail since 12.12.2022 and in case, he is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in trial.
5. Learned AGA appearing for State and learned counsel for Informant submit that victim has received six injuries which could be attributed to iron rod allegedly assigned to applicant.
Victim in her statement has made allegation of attempt to rape also and since statement of victim is yet to be recorded during trial, therefore, bail may not be granted.
6. LAW ON BAIL - A SUMMARY (A) The basic rule may perhaps be tersely put as bail, not jail.

(B) Power to grant bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C., is of wide amplitude but not an unfettered discretion, which calls for exercise in a judicious manner and not as a matter of course or in whimsical manner.

(C) While passing an order on an application for grant of bail, there is no need to record elaborate details to give an impression that the case is one that would result in a conviction or, by contrast, in an acquittal.

However, a Court cannot completely divorce its decision from material aspects of the case such as allegations made against accused; nature and gravity of accusation; having common object or intention; severity of punishment if allegations are proved beyond reasonable doubt and would result in a conviction; reasonable apprehension of witnesses being influenced by accused;
tampering of evidence; character, behaviour, means, position and standing of accused; likelihood of offence being repeated; the frivolity in the case of prosecution; criminal antecedents of accused and a prima facie satisfaction of Court in support of charge against accused.

The Court may also take note of participation or part of an unlawful assembly as well as that circumstantial evidence not being a ground to grant bail, if the evidence/ material collected establishes prima facie a complete chain of events.
Parity may not be an only ground but remains a relevant factor for consideration of application for bail.

(D) Over crowding of jail and gross delay in disposal of cases when undertrials are forced to remain in jail (not due to their fault) may give rise to possible situations that may justify invocation of Article 21 of Constitution, may also be considered along with other factors.

sentences.text: In the present case victim herself has lodged FIR still there was a delay of two days.

She has improved her case in statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. that applicant and co-accused not only assaulted her and her son but also tried to raped her whereas earlier her case was confined to allegation of assault and outrage of modesty.
Motive assigned appears not to be sufficient.

However, medical evidence corroborated with allegation of assault, i.e., an offence under Section 323 IPC.
8.

In these circumstances, considering relevant factors, such as, improvement by victim in prosecution case; nature of evidence with regard to motive; offence under Section 323 IPC is bailable; co-accused has already been granted bail by this Court though reasons given therein may not be in terms of judgment passed by Supreme Court in Manoj Kumar Khokhar (supra) and Brijmani Devi vs. Pappu Kumar (2022) 4 SCC 497; applicant is in jail since 12.12.2022; trial is proceeding in a snail speed and there is overcrowding in jail, a case of bail is made out.

sentences.text: 9. However, applicant is directed to remain present on each and every date as and when required by Trial Court during trial and in case any application for exemption on vague ground is filed, the same shall be a ground for Trial Court to cancel bail immediately.

10. Let the applicant-Rajkumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
(ii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment or exemption from appearance on the date fixed in trial.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iii) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
(iv) The Trial Court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously, preferably within a period of six months after release of applicant,
Rajkumar vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124661895/
3 if there is no other legal impediment.

11. The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
12. The bail application is allowed.
13. It is made clear that the observations made hereinabove are only for the purpose of adjudicating the present bail application.
